newsitem.title: UK: Smiths sees further profits growth ahead.
newsitem.headline: Smiths sees further profits growth ahead.

text.p: Avionics, medical and industrial products group Smiths Industries Plc announced a 19 percent rise in profits on Wednesday and said it expected growth to continue, helped by acquisitions and an upturn in the aerospace industry.

Pretax profits for the year to August 3 rose to 165.4 million pounds ($261.8 million) on sales up 12 percent at 1.08 billion pounds. The total dividend was raised 12.5 percent to 16.2 pence a share, on earnings up 24 percent at 36.6 pence.
Operating profits rose to 168.1 million pounds from 140.9 million pounds last time.

Smiths spent 98 million pounds buying three companies for the medical and industrial divisions last year, but stripping out acquisitions made in the last two years underlying profits were still up 14 percent across the group, chairman Sir Roger Hurn said.
"Overall I have confidence in the outlook for increases in sales, profits, earnings per share and dividends in the years ahead," Hurn said.
"With renewed optimism about aerospace, the prospects for all three groups are very good and I am confident we can deliver further gains in profits and earnings per share."

Hurn said he hoped to continue the strategy of expanding the medical and industrial divisions through bolt-on acquisitions, but would not rule out making a major acquisition to establish a fourth division if the right opportunity arose.

"Maybe, if the right thing comes up, but...in the meantime we are very happy to go on growing the business at the sort of rates we are achieving at the present time," he told Reuters in an interview. He said he could not comment on whether or not Smiths had any major takeover targets in sight.
Two acquisitions helped boost operating profits at the Industrial division to 49.7 million pounds from 37.6 million a year ago, on sales up 31 percent at 328 million poounds.
Medical Systems saw operating profits rise to 73.1 million pounds from 63 million pounds last time on sales up 10 percent at 275.4 million pounds.
Meanwhile Hurn said the avionics business continued to improve margins last year and he was now looking towards the long awaited upturn in the aircraft manufacturing industry.
Aerospace made an operating profit in the year just ended of 45.3 million pounds, up from 40.3 million last time, on flat sales of 377.1 million pounds.
"We kept our aerospace group on a tight rein during the recession and even a modest improvement in sales will enhance profits," Hurn said.
However, new airline orders for aircraft have yet to feed through to production runs and Hurn said he did not expect to see any major upturn for Smiths sales for another 12 months.
For the current year he also warned that that the recent three-month strike at the military aircraft division of McDonnell Douglas was likely to have an impact on the division's results this year.

McDonnell Douglas had continued to take Smiths avionics for its F-18, T45 Goshawk and Harrier AV8-B aircraft during the dispute at its St Louis plant, which was settled a month ago, but Smiths fears that Douglas will want to slow down further supplies until it catches up on its production schedule.

"Like all aircraft manufacturers they want to go on delivering during a strike and then they adjust their schedules later," he said. "We are still waiting to see the impact of these adjustments but we expect to see the impact in our next two quarters perhaps."
McDonnell Douglas had said last month that it managed to keep production going during the strike at nearly normal rates by using white collar staff and temporary replacement workers. ($1=.6317 Pound)
